title: Winter hill trip outfits: what to pack for the mountains
excerpt: Planning a December trip to the hills? Here's how to layer tees, hoodies and sweatshirts, plus a simple 5-day packing list.
content:
December plans ban rahe hain? Whether it is a snowy weekend in the mountains, a long Himachal or Uttarakhand road trip, or a quiet stay in a hill town with chai and views, one question comes up every time: kya pack karein? Pack too little and you shiver. Pack too much and you carry a heavy bag up every staircase. This guide keeps it simple, practical and comfortable.

The golden rule: layers, not one heavy jacket

Hill weather changes fast. The afternoon sun can feel warm, and an hour later the wind turns cold. That is why layering works better than one thick jacket. You add or remove pieces as the day changes, and every piece gets used more than once.

A simple three-layer system works for most winter trips:

  • Base layer: a soft cotton T-shirt or thermal next to your skin.
  • Mid layer: a hoodie or sweatshirt that holds warmth.
  • Outer layer: a windproof or padded jacket for nights, snow and high passes.

Base layer: start with good cotton tees

Your T-shirt is the piece that touches your skin all day, so comfort matters most here. Our regular tees are 180 GSM and our oversized tees are 240 GSM, both in 100% super-combed cotton, bio-washed and pre-shrunk. They feel soft, breathe well while you walk, and don't lose their shape after a few washes on the trip.

A small tip: if you plan to layer a hoodie on top, a regular fit tee sits more neatly underneath. An oversized tee is great on its own for sunny afternoons, cafe-hopping and photos, and it still works under an open jacket. Pack 3 to 4 tees for a week; you can repeat them since the outer layers do most of the "looking good" work.

Mid layer: the hoodie and sweatshirt do the real work

This is your most-used piece on a hill trip. A 300 GSM fleece hoodie or sweatshirt keeps you warm on morning walks, inside chilly homestays and on long drives. Fleece is soft on the inside and holds body heat well.

  • Hoodie: the hood helps a lot when the wind picks up at viewpoints or in the evening. Pair it with a beanie and you are sorted.
  • Sweatshirt: a clean crew neck that layers easily under a jacket and looks neat for dinners and cafes.

Ideally carry one of each, ya phir two hoodies in different colours so your photos don't all look the same. Darker shades also hide road-trip dust better.

Outer layer and bottoms

For places with snow or very cold nights, a proper padded or windproof jacket is a must. Wear it on top of your hoodie, not instead of it. For bottoms, carry one pair of comfortable jeans or cargos and one pair of joggers or sweatpants. Joggers are perfect for long bus or car journeys and for lounging at the homestay in the evening.

Don't forget the small things

  • Warm socks: at least one pair of woollen socks for nights.
  • Beanie, gloves and a muffler: small, light, and they make a big difference.
  • Good shoes: sneakers with grip, or trekking shoes if you plan to walk on snow.
  • A tote bag: handy as a day bag for local markets, snacks and a water bottle, and it folds flat in your suitcase.
  • Sunscreen and lip balm: mountain sun is strong even when it is cold.

A simple packing list for a 5-day trip

  1. 3 to 4 cotton T-shirts (regular or oversized)
  2. 2 hoodies or sweatshirts
  3. 1 warm outer jacket
  4. 1 pair of jeans or cargos and 1 pair of joggers
  5. 1 set of thermals for very cold nights
  6. Socks, beanie, gloves and a muffler
  7. 1 foldable tote bag

Everything on this list mixes and matches, so you can create a new look each day without overpacking.
